defect.evidence_quote: We here consider only searches carried out by school authorities acting alone and on their own authority.
defect.locator_note: holding frontmatter; limitation appears in cached opinion footnote 7
defect.problem: The holding is supported in substance but is overbroad and truncated as framed: it omits that T.L.O. addressed public school authorities acting alone/on their own authority, and the scope prong is left as 'reasonably…'.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: A public school official acting alone/on school authority may search a student under a reasonableness-under-all-the-circumstances standard; ordinarily the search must be justified at inception and reasonably related in scope, without a warrant or probable cause.

reasons: The opinion supports the core rule: legality of a student search depends on reasonableness under all the circumstances, not strict probable cause.
The opinion supports the twofold inquiry: justified at inception and reasonably related in scope.
Footnote 7 expressly excludes searches with or at the behest of law enforcement, so the unqualified 'school official's search' phrasing should be narrowed.
residual_risks: The visible holding text is truncated with an ellipsis, so the full intended frontmatter proposition cannot be verified beyond the disclosed text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Add 'public' and 'acting alone/on school authority,' and spell out 'reasonably related in scope.'

reasons: The lake treatment scope note calls the case an anchor for the reasonableness standard governing school searches.

The opinion applies a reasonableness balancing approach, rejects warrant/probable-cause requirements for school searches, and refers to the special needs of the school environment in the disclosed text.
residual_risks: The separate home page file was not disclosed, so the home taxonomy itself was not independently audited.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Specify that the anchor role is for public-school search reasonableness within the special-needs/administrative-search family.
